extracted.intended_audience: novelists, fiction-writers, literary critics and students of the novel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the formal principles that should govern a novel: unity of subject and form, scope, treatment of time and space, point of view, and how episodes and characters must serve the central design. Uses close reading of War and Peace as examples of good and flawed practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and subject unity
rubrics_metrics.description: "The best form is that which makes the most of its subject... The well-made book is the book in which the subject and the form coincide and are indistinguishable — the book in which the matter is all used up in the form, in which the form expresses all the matter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form should express all the matter; if form and subject disagree there will be superfluous or missing material and the story will suffer. Aim for a form that uses every part of the material to serve the subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifiable subject (expressible succinctly)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If it cannot be put into a phrase it is no subject for a novel... It may be the simplest anecdote or the most elaborate concatenation of events, it may be a solitary figure or the widest network of relationships; it is anyhow expressible in ten words that reveal its unity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine a clear, concise statement of the novel's subject early; the form of the book depends on knowing that subject. Without a phraseable subject there is nothing firm to shape the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single centre / unifying design
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel should possess a centre: avoid a "confusion of two designs"—writing "two novels at once"—which produces a book with no centre and undermines unity (illustrated by the coexistence of the "youth and age" story and the "war and peace" story in War and Peace).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose one unifying design or intentionally devise a scheme that unites multiple themes; do not allow two large, independent subjects to coexist without a deliberate organizing principle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope and scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Some subjects "require a generous amount of room" — e.g., a theme about the march of generations needs a big and various population, open space, and time to be convincingly treated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the novel's length, cast size, temporal span, and spatial breadth to the demands of the subject. Neither artificially truncate a theme nor bloat a small subject into undue expanses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy of material / avoid wastefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Tolstoy’s novel is wasteful of its subject... Where there is disagreement and conflict between the two, there is stuff that is superfluous or there is stuff that is wanting."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every scene, digression and character should contribute toward the subject; excise material that does not serve the book's central purpose and develop material that is necessary but under-treated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance of episodes; avoid irrelevant digressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Interminable chapters of comment or explanation ("pamphleteering", e.g., "the historians") interrupt and damage the narrative; the reader often skips such sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid authorial interruptions that explain or theorize at length; ensure episodes and expository passages advance or deepen the principal story rather than distract from it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of narrative point of view
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of scenes differs when Tolstoy is "immediately beside us, narrating" versus when "Peter and Andrew... are with us and about us, and Tolstoy is effaced." He sometimes "chooses his onlooker at random and follows no consistent method."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt and maintain a coherent method of narration (direct narrator, focalization through characters, chosen onlooker). Inconsistent shifting of perspective can fracture the book's unity and confuse the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters should embody and clarify the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: "Figures are sought and chosen for the clarity with which the drama is embodied in them... Essentially they are not princes, not Russians, but figures in the great procession."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and develop characters because they represent and illuminate the central theme; favor representative, typical figures when the subject calls for universality rather than parochial specificity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of large cast and complex events
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in a panoramic novel there must be no faltering in hold upon character: "he never loses his way among the scores of men and women... in all the endless series of scenes and events there is not one which betrays a hesitating intention."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clarity and authorial control when dealing with many characters and episodes: each part should feel purposeful and placed, so the reader does not question direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sense of space and continuity (setting/horizon)
rubrics_metrics.description: The continuity of space and daylight is necessary to Tolstoy’s motive: his people "move in an atmosphere that knows no limit... The horizon of a Russian story would naturally be vague and vast." (Contrast with Dostoevsky’s enclosed, dark staging.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide how expansive or closed the novel’s world should be; render a convincing sense of space (open horizons or confined interiors) that supports the theme and allows characters to belong plausibly to a larger life or an enclosed arena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of time (the form of time)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The form of time is to be represented, and that is something more than to represent its contents in their order... The lines and masses of the book must show it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the passage and sweep of time perceptible through the book's structure, pacing, and arrangement of scenes rather than relying on summary announcements. The shape of the narrative should embody temporal movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper grouping and proportion of thematic material
rubrics_metrics.description: The "cycle of war and peace... is broken and fragmentary" and "are not properly grouped and composed," producing fragments adjusted to incompatible points of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group related episodes and scenes so that thematic cycles are coherent and proportioned; avoid scattering related material in ways that prevent a full treatment of a theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fully develop principal themes (avoid incompleteness)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each of [the two themes] is incomplete; neither of them is given its full development, for all the size of the book."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that central thematic threads receive complete development; a large canvas does not absolve the need to finish the thematic work you set out to do.
